proposals.before: His younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou, was widely thought to surpass Xin in reputation.
proposals.after: His younger brother Hui, courtesy name Jingyou; worldly praise mostly favored Xin.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世譽多欣 means contemporary praise mostly went to Xin, not that Hui surpassed Xin; the literal field is correct.

proposals.before: Recently He Jianchuo sent your letter; though I know it was in jest, I know you truly cannot pity me.
proposals.after: Recently I saw Jianchuo deliver your letter; though I know it was in jest, I know you truly cannot pity me.
proposals.reason: 綽 is Wang Sengchuo elsewhere; 何見 is 'how/when I saw', not a surname He attached to Jianchuo.

proposals.before: When he saw his father's younger brother's wife he was often moved to grief and choked with sobs.
proposals.after: When he saw his maternal aunt (from-mother) he was often moved to grief and choked with sobs.
proposals.reason: 從母 is the mother's sister (maternal aunt), not father's younger brother's wife.

proposals.before: Past noon he did not come—I was already weary with hope; now how can I stand? Examining myself, dim poison—no more human reason.
proposals.after: Past noon he did not come—I was already weary with longing; now how can I stand? Examining myself in dim anguish—I am no longer within human norms.
proposals.reason: 惛毒 means confused/dim anguish of grief, not literal poison; 愒望 is weary longing; 無復人理 means no longer within human norms.

proposals.before: If my thoughts cannot be fulfilled, Xie can think of it like madness, not knowing whom to tell; plainly writing these sheets without order or reason, briefly tracing our paths—of ten thousand things not one is written.
proposals.after: If my thoughts find no outlet, Xie may ponder them in frenzy, not knowing whom to tell; plainly writing these sheets without order or reason, briefly tracing our paths—of ten thousand things not one is written.
proposals.reason: 意慮不遂 means thoughts find no outlet/fulfillment; 思之如狂 is to ponder in frenzy—current phrasing is unclear about Xie's role.

proposals.after: Chief Clerk He was Yan (He Yan).
proposals.reason: 偃 is the given name of 何偃; bare 'Yan' obscures the surname already established by 何長史.

decisions.reason: 世譽多欣 means worldly praise mostly favored Xin; the before text reverses the comparison and invents Hui surpassing Xin.

decisions.after: Recently I saw Chuo deliver your letter; though I know it was in jest, I know you truly cannot pity me.
decisions.reason: 何見綽 is 'saw Chuo', not a surname He or a compound Jianchuo; 何見 is the seeing, and 綽 alone names the courier (Wang Sengchuo).

decisions.after: When he saw his maternal aunt he was often moved to grief and choked with sobs.
decisions.reason: 從母 is the mother's sister (maternal aunt), not father's younger brother's wife; drop the awkward parenthetical while keeping that sense.
愒望 is weary longing, 惛毒 is dim anguish of grief rather than literal poison, and 無復人理 means no longer within human norms.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 已自愒望……自省惛毒，無復人理

decisions.reason: 意慮不遂 and 謝能思之如狂 are already rendered accurately enough; 'find no outlet' and 'ponder them in frenzy' are stylistic rewrites, not error fixes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 儻意慮不遂，謝能思之如狂

decisions.reason: 何長史者，偃也 literally identifies him as Yan after 何長史 already supplies the surname; the parenthetical He Yan is an idiomatic gloss, not a literal correction.

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0002 shows English Jianchuo came only from fusing 見綽; the alternate-name claim for 綽 must read Chuo while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
